```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(raster)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(dplyr)
library(ggspatial)
library(ggplot2)
library(tibble)
library(ggthemes)
library(geodata)
library(psych)
library(ggfortify)
```

# Collect Environmental Data for Populations

Here, we extract the bioclim variables for the populations of EUVI for which we have genomic data. We are using a 30 second resolution of the bioclim variables. 

```{r}
locations <- read.delim("data/EUVI_locations.txt", header =T)

# Filter locations to only samples that we are using: 

popmap3 <- read.delim("data/samples_to_keep.txt", sep = " ")

locations_update <- distinct(locations[locations$EUVI_Sample %in% popmap3$V1,])
loc_lat_long <- locations_update %>% 
  dplyr::select(Lat, Long)
loc_lat_long$Lat <- as.numeric(loc_lat_long$Lat)
loc_lat_long$Long <- as.numeric(loc_lat_long$Long)

loc_sp <- SpatialPoints(loc_lat_long)
coordinates(loc_lat_long) <- ~ Long + Lat
myCRS1 <- CRS("WGS84") # WGS 84
crs(loc_lat_long) <- myCRS1

map = ne_countries(scale = 10, returnclass = "sf")
reprojected_map <- sf::st_transform(map, 'WGS84')

ggplot() + geom_sf(data = reprojected_map, color = "black", size = 0.05, fill = "white") + theme_classic() +
  coord_sf(xlim=c(-130, 75), ylim=c(0, 60)) +
  geom_point(data = locations_update, mapping = aes(x= Long, y=Lat))
  
#ggsave("global_map2.pdf", width = 12, height = 10)

# Do this once: 

#worldclim_global(var = "bio",res = "0.5", path = "./")

# search files with .tif file extension
# These files are NOT included in the /data directory and should be downloaded from worldclim using the line above 

clim_list <- list.files("../climate/wc2.1_30s/",pattern=".tif",full.names = T)
# stacking the bioclim variables to process them at one go 
clim <- raster::stack(clim_list) 

#plot(clim) # we don't need to plot the clim layers, but good to check just in case 

conditions_occ <- extract(clim,loc_lat_long)
#head(conditions_occ)

plot(clim$wc2.1_30s_bio_1)
plot(loc_lat_long,add=T)

conditions_occs_df <- as.data.frame(conditions_occ)
colnames(conditions_occs_df) <- c("bio1", "bio10", "bio11", "bio12", "bio13", "bio14", "bio15", "bio16", "bio17", 
                                  "bio18", "bio19", "bio2", "bio3", "bio4", "bio5", "bio6", "bio7", "bio8", 
                                  "bio9")
occs_envir <- cbind(locations_update, conditions_occs_df)

#write.table(file = "individual_climate_data_30s.txt",occs_envir, quote = F, row.names = F)
```

**Summary:** Starting with the 19 bioclimatic variables from the WorldClim2 dataset, we need to first remove strong correlations between predictors. Here, we start by looking the pairwise Pearson correlation coefficients (top right), histograms for each variable (center diagonal), and scatterplots (bottom left). Then we generate a PCA for the environmental predictors from which we can decide which predictors to include in the genotype-environment association models. 

Based on the results below, we decided to keep:

* Maximum temperature of warmest month (Bio5) and minimum temperature of coldest month (Bio6) reflect extremes in temperature that would limit the insect’s distribution in very cold and hot areas. Adult <i>E. villosus</i> overwinter in soil litter and cracks in the soil surface and so would likely be impacted by freezing conditions even during diapause (Fornasari & Sobhian, 1993). 

* Precipitation of coldest quarter (Bio19) and precipitation of driest quarter (Bio17) are likely to have indirect impacts on <i>E. villosus</i> through <i>C. solstitialis </i>, the host plant. Prolonged freezing temperatures and ice accumulation can reduce or kill developing flower buds and reduce overwintering survival rates (Roché et al., 1997; Gutierrez et al., 2017). Likewise, prolonged and severe droughts can lead to high plant mortality (Sheley & Larson, 1994; Enloe et al., 2004). 

* Finally, mean diurnal range [(mean of monthly (max temp - min temp))] (Bio2) captures the variation in temperatures experienced across <i>E. villosus</i>’s distribution. 


```{r}
### examine correlations between bioclimatic variables from WorldClim2
# read in data
env <- read.delim("data/individual_climate_data_30s.txt", sep = " ")
env$Site <- as.character(env$Site)

# visualize correlated variables via pairwise comparisons
pairs.panels(env[,5:23], scale=T, gap=0, method="pearson")

```
Let's make a PCA of the bioclim variables. 

```{r}
env2 <- env[,5:23]
rownames(env2) <- env$EUVI_Sample

#run with princomp
normalized_env2 <- scale(env2)

#env_pop <- distinct()

pca <- princomp(normalized_env2, scale = T)
summary(pca)
loadings<- pca$loadings

autoplot(pca, loadings = T, loadings.label = T, loadings.label.colour = "darkblue", loadings.colour = "darkblue" ) + theme_bw()



# run with prcomp
#pca <- prcomp(env_pop, scale = T)
#summary(pca)

#autoplot(pca, loadings = T, loadings.label = T, loadings.label.colour = "darkblue", loadings.colour = "darkblue" ) + theme_bw()
#barplot(pca$rotation[,1], main = "")

```
**Environmental Clines**: For each bioclimatic variable, look at the clines in the Introduced (introduced) and Native (native). 

```{r, fig.height=4, fig.width=5}
bio1 <- clim[[1]]
# Plot Introduced 
plot(bio1, xlim = c(-130,-100), ylim = c(25, 50), main = "Bio1 Introduced")
plot(loc_lat_long,add=T, pch = 16, cex = 0.5)

# Plot Greece/Turkey
plot(bio1, xlim = c(15,60), ylim = c(30, 50), main = "Bio1 Native")
plot(loc_lat_long,add=T, pch = 16, cex = 0.5)

WUS <- filter(env, Long < 0) %>% 
  select(bio1)

knitr::kable(summary(WUS), caption = "Summary of bioclim variable for Introduced Sampling Sites", )


EU <- filter(env, Long > 0) %>% 
  select(bio1)

knitr::kable(summary(EU), caption = "Summary of bioclim variable for Native Sampling Sites")


```
